- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–30% in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast mid-point if sentiment drops below 0.3.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.50” values, model tends to lag; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is uniformly positive (e.g., 1.00 for 5+ days), model often overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 10% below 30-day true high.
